questions.html: Buffer is required at receiver side of data link layer. What is its purpose?

options.html: To accept out of order data frames and hold it temporarily for sorting.
To discard out of order frames.

questions.solution:
(a)
Requirement of buffer for holding out of order data is for applying sorting logic and giving as inorder data to above layers.

questions.html: The number of links used in half duplex in point to point link
questions.solution:
(a)
In half duplex, once data is transmitted, same link can be used for sending ack as the link is free so number of links is 1.

questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : DNS can use either of TCP or UDP, for its query and response messages.
S2 : SMTP is not used for transferring e-mail messages from the recipients’s mail server to the recipients’s personal computer.
S3 : HTTP can use multiple TCP connections between the same client and the server.
S4 : POP protocol is used to download an E-mail from mailbox server to a mail client.
Which of the above statement are correct?
questions.solution:
(d)
• TCP involves a connection establishment phase while UDP does not. Using TCP for DNS may
end up involving several TCP connections to be established since several name server may
have to be contacted to translate a name into an IP address. This imposes a high overhead in
delay. Hence DNS uses UDP for its query and response messages.
• SMTP is a push protocol, whereas the given task is pull operation.
• S3 and S4 statements are correct.

questions.html: In P-persistent CSMA network there are 6 systems in a slot. The probability of each station sending the data is 0.7 and to avoid collision only 2 stations should transmit the data at a time. What is the probability that channel is collision free? ________ (Upto three decimal places)
Consider different activities related to e-mail. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.html: Sending an e-mail from a mail client to a mail server uses SMTP protocol.
Sending an e-mail from a mail client to a mail server uses POP protocol.
Downloading an e-mail from mailbox server to a mail client uses POP protocol.
Downloading an e-mail from mailbox server to a mail client uses SMTP protocol.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
• SMTP (simple mail transfer protocol) typically used by user client for sending mails.
• POP (post office protocol) used by client for receiving mails.

questions.html:
Consider a network connecting two systems located 4000 kilometers apart. The bandwidth of the network is 64 Mbps. The propagation speed of the media is 2/3 of the speed of light in vacuum.
It is needed to design selective repeat sliding window protocol for this network. The average packet size is of 8 Kb. The network is to be used to its full capacity.
Assume that processing delays at nodes are negligible. Then, the minimum size in bits of the sequence number field has to be _________.

Consider the following statements:
(a) Hidden terminals can be handled by using either of RTS or CTS control frame.
(b) RTS/CTS exchange helps in reducing collisions and leads to efficient use of channel resources.
(c) 802.11 frame has three address fields.
(d) By the help of 802.11 frame, we can come to known whether encryption is used on not.
Which of the above statement is correct?
questions.solution:
(d)
• Both RTS and CTS control frames are required to deal with hidden terminals.
• RTS/CTS exchange can help reduce collisions but consume channel resources.
• 802.11 frame has 4 address fields.
• WEP field of 802.11 frame indicates whether encryption is being used or not.
